close_reason: wontfix: bikeshedding. Epic JMAP-6r7c explicitly flagged this as bikeshedding ('SseFrame.id conflation' in the opinion bucket). RFC 8895 §9.2 distinguishes 'id field not present' from 'bare id: (reset)'. Real-world JMAP push streams send id: <value> on every event; the bare-reset case is theoretical. Distinguishing it would require Option<Option<String>> or a three-variant enum on the public SseFrame.id field, which trades a real shape complication for a theoretical wire-format edge case no JMAP server emits. Re-file with concrete evidence if a deployed JMAP server is observed to send bare id: lines.
description:
sse.rs:13-34 — pub struct SseFrame { pub event: SseEvent, pub id: Option<String> }

The struct-level doc-comment (sse.rs:13-24) explicitly states the limitation:
"This implementation conflates the first two cases: both produce id: None."

Where the three RFC 8895 §9.2 states are:
1. No id: field present → unchanged
2. Bare id: field (no value) → RESET to empty
3. id: value → updated to value

The conflation is intentional and documented. For JMAP's actual use case (Last-Event-ID reconnection), the distinction rarely matters because servers rarely emit a bare-id reset frame mid-stream.

But the contract gap: callers implementing strict RFC 8895 §9.2 reconnect semantics cannot distinguish. A future minor release that wanted to expose the distinction would have to break the type:
  pub enum SseFrameId { Unchanged, Reset, Set(String) }

The current `Option<String>` is committed; changing it is a breaking change.

For the foundation library, the right call may be to commit now to "JMAP-flavor SSE only, never strict RFC 8895" — which is what the type does, just be explicit about it. OR to introduce the tri-state type now while the crate is still 0.x.

Recommendation: low priority. The current conflation is documented and acceptable for JMAP. Filing so the future-major-version conversation has a record.
title: SseFrame.id conflates 'no id field present' with 'bare id: (reset)' — RFC 8895 §9.2 distinguishes
